children: Wall Street was mixed on Tuesday as the rally in technology stocks continued to push the Nasdaq Composite to new all-time trading highs.
The blue-chip Dow
was last -0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) was last +0.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (
) was last +0.2%.
Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:
Shopify partners with Meta on AI shopping while Amazon blocks tool:
Shopify
rose more than 5% in premarket trading after announcing a partnership with Meta

to enable AI agent Muse to complete purchases through Shop Pay on all Shopify stores. "We are partnering deeply with Muse to enable agentic checkout with Shop Pay on all Shopify stores, offering people an easy and delightful way to shop and check out with Muse," said Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke. The move comes as Amazon

blocked Muse and other AI shopping bots—including OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, and Perplexity's Comet—from its retail platform, citing concerns that third-party bots could bypass its native storefront and jeopardize its advertising business.
Crude oil drops below $100 as Iran signals potential diplomacy:
Brent crude fell

$100 per barrel for a fifth consecutive session following reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. lifts its blockade. Front-month Nymex crude declined 0.8% to $94.97/bbl while Brent dropped 1.1% to $99.26/bbl. Iranian state-affiliated media later denied the claim, limiting further declines. Separately, Saudi Arabia has restarted operations at its damaged East-West pipeline and aims to resume exports via the Yanbu port on the Red Sea later this week at reduced volume, providing an alternative route to bypass Strait of Hormuz disruptions.
Microsoft cuts 268 Xbox jobs and transfers 'Halo' development to Activision:
Microsoft's

Xbox division is  eliminating 268 positions and reorganizing several game studios, with Activision taking responsibility for developing the next "Halo" title, according to a staff memo from Xbox Chief Content Officer Matt Booty. The cuts affect Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and Xbox Game Studios management. Under the reorganization, Activision will also oversee World's Edge and Rare, while Bethesda takes responsibility for Obsidian, King adds Microsoft Casual Games to its operations, and Playground and Turn 10 combine into a single studio focused on the "Forza" and "Fable" franchises. The actions follow Xbox's July announcement of plans to cut as many as 3,200 jobs, roughly 20% of its workforce.
Novo Nordisk considers hair-loss space in post-Wegovy strategy:
Novo Nordisk

executives  signaled potential interest in expanding into the hair-loss market as the Ozempic maker seeks to diversify beyond GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. "We could leverage our scientific knowledge potentially moving into that space," Chief Scientific Officer Martin Lange told Bloomberg. The remarks boosted shares of hair-loss drug developers Veradermics and Absci. No FDA-approved therapies for pattern hair loss—affecting an estimated 50 million men and 30 million women in the U.S.—have emerged since the 1990s. Novo Nordisk has faced increasing pressure from rival Eli Lilly in the injectable GLP-1 market and a looming patent cliff beyond 2030 threatens its best-selling semaglutide drugs.
